title:
And they call me the jewel of Asia,
 Of Asia,
 The Geisha.
html_source:
Lyrics from ‘The Geisha, a Story of a Tea House’ (1896), a musical comedy.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Geisha

Presumably, this what Mr Cunningham’s wife was singing while drunk.

In the next line, Bloom suspects that Cunningham “knows.”

Perhaps this thought of Mr. Cunningham’s intemperate wife has led Bloom to think again about Molly’s upcoming infidelity, and then to a (somewhat paranoid) suspicion that Cunningham knows about it as well.

Or, more likely, a much less paranoid suspicion that Cunningham knows about Bloom’s father’s suicide. This is why Cunningham cut short the other men’s discussion of suicide, as Cunningham confirms in his quick aside with Mr Power in the cemetery.

It seems no matter how he tries, Bloom cannot distract himself from things he does not want to think about: his father’s death, his son’s death, and Molly’s infidelity.
